s: With whom is the concept of the 'primate city' associated?
x: Mark Jefferson defined a primate city as several times larger than the next city.

s: What does the German term 'Umland' refer to?
o: A chain of merged metropolitan areas
The area surrounding a town and linked to it
A city several times larger than the next
A city of 10 million or more
x: Umland is the area surrounding a town and linked to it, its hinterland (UPPSC 2017).

s: Under Article 243P, what population must an area have to be a metropolitan area?
x: Article 243P defines a metropolitan area as having 10 lakh or more people.

s: The slum population constituted approximately what percentage of India's urban population according to Census 2011?
x: Slum dwellers accounted for about 17.4% of India's urban population in Census 2011.

s: Among million-plus cities in Census 2011, which had the highest share of slum households?
x: Greater Visakhapatnam (about 44%) was ahead of Mumbai (about 41%), though Greater Mumbai had the largest slum population.

s: In Census 2011, which State had the highest share of its urban population living in slums?
x: Undivided Andhra Pradesh had the highest share, at about 36%.

s: Which State had the largest number of slum dwellers in Census 2011?
x: Maharashtra had the largest slum number; undivided AP had the highest slum share (~36%).

s: Which city had the largest number of slum dwellers in Census 2011?
x: Greater Mumbai had the largest number; Greater Visakhapatnam had the highest share (~44%).

s: Using a broader definition, how many slum dwellers does the World Bank estimate India has?
x: The World Bank puts slum dwellers at 177 million, against the Census figure of 6.54 crore.

s: Which of the following is a major cause of urban flooding in expanding cities?
o: Construction over lakes, wetlands and floodplains
x: Urban flooding is caused by construction over water bodies and floodplains, concretisation of permeable soil and blocked drains.

s: Which of the following causes the urban heat island effect?
o: Low building density, irrigated fields and cool winds
Open wetlands, permeable soil and increased tree cover
Dense construction, asphalt surfaces and loss of tree cover
Reduced construction, bare rock and expanded forests
x: Dense construction, asphalt and the loss of tree cover trap heat and intensify the urban heat island effect.

s: India generates about how much municipal solid waste a year?
x: India generates about 62 million tonnes of MSW a year; about 70% is collected but only 30% processed.

s: How many of the world's ten most polluted cities are in India?
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Five); it is added as option 5.
IQAir's World Air Quality Report 2025 (24 Mar 2026) has 5 Indian cities in the world's top 10; the old figure 'eight' is not supported (2019: six).

s: Against one per 5,000 in developed countries, India has about one urban planner per how many people?
x: India has approximately one planner per one lakh people, whereas developed countries have about one per 5,000.

s:
Consider the following statements about municipal solid waste in India:
1. About 62 million tonnes are generated a year.
2. About 70% of it is processed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: India generates about 62 million tonnes a year; about 70% is collected but only 30% processed.

s: Which of the following is NOT a measure to prevent urban flooding?
x: Building basements does not control floods; protecting wetlands, clear drains and open floodplains do.

s: Which is the most polluted capital city in the world?
x: Delhi is the most polluted capital, and 8 of the world's 10 most polluted cities are in India.

s: Jakarta replaced Tokyo as the world's most populous city in WUP 2025 mainly because of:
o: a change in Japan's census year
the merger of Jakarta with neighbouring provinces
x: The change is attributed to the new city-definition method adopted in World Urbanisation Prospects 2025, not to a demographic collapse of Tokyo.

s: According to the World Urbanization Prospects 2025, which is the world's most populous city?
x: The order is Jakarta, Dhaka, Tokyo and New Delhi.

s: What is New Delhi's rank in the UN DESA World Urbanization Prospects 2025?
x: WUP 2025 ranks Jakarta 1st, Dhaka, Tokyo and New Delhi 4th.

s: What is India's urban population projected to reach by 2050?
x: India's urban population is projected at 951 million by 2050.

s: In the earlier UN lists of the world's largest cities, which rank did Delhi hold after Tokyo?
x: Earlier lists had Tokyo 1st and Delhi 2nd, with Mumbai 7th and Kolkata 10th.

s: In the UN lists of the world's largest cities before WUP 2025, which city was ranked first?
x: Earlier UN lists ranked Tokyo first and Delhi second; WUP 2025's new method puts Jakarta first.

s: According to the World Urbanization Prospects 2025, which city is the world's second most populous?
x: WUP 2025 ranks Jakarta first, Dhaka second, Tokyo third and New Delhi fourth.

s: According to the World Urbanization Prospects 2025, what share of the world's 8.2 billion people live in cities?
x: WUP 2025 says cities hold 45% of the world's 8.2 billion people.

s: Which authority plans the Chennai Metropolitan Area?
x: Chennai is planned by CMDA (1974); KMDA (1970) is Kolkata's, VMRDA plans Visakhapatnam and APCRDA plans Amaravati.

s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, how have 16 major Indian cities grown during 2000-2020?
o: vertical, with the core growing faster than the periphery
horizontal, with the periphery growing faster than the core
horizontal, with the core growing faster than the periphery
vertical, with the periphery growing faster than the core
x: The periphery grew faster than the core and expansion was predominantly horizontal; the administrative city no longer matches the economic metropolitan region.

s: Which pair of planning authority and year of establishment is correctly matched?
x: KMDA was established in 1970; MMRDA in 1975, CMDA in 1974 and DDA in 1957.

s: In which year was the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) set up?
x: MMRDA was set up in 1975, after DDA (1957), KMDA (1970) and CMDA (1974).

s: Which authority plans the Visakhapatnam metropolitan region?
x: VMRDA plans Visakhapatnam; APCRDA runs Amaravati.

s: Which Article provides for a Metropolitan Planning Committee for every metropolitan area?
x: Article 243ZE provides for Metropolitan Planning Committees; Article 243P defines a metropolitan area.

s: The 74th Amendment, 1992 inserted which Part into the Constitution?
x: The 74th Amendment inserted Part IXA on municipalities.

s: Swachh Survekshan began in 2016 with how many cities?
x: It began in 2016 with 73 cities; run by MoHUA and conducted by QCI, the 2024-25 survey covered 4,589 cities.

s: Which cities were listed in the Super Swachh League (10 lakh+ population) of Swachh Survekshan?
x: Indore, Surat and Navi Mumbai were in the 10 lakh+ Super Swachh League; Noida, Chandigarh and Mysuru in its 3-10 lakh category.

s: Which of the following cities is included among the newer Tier-2 cities topping the Ease of Living Index?
x: Pune, Navi Mumbai and Tirupati are identified among the newer Tier-2 cities topping the Ease of Living Index.

s: Which body conducts Swachh Survekshan for the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs?
x: The Quality Council of India conducts Swachh Survekshan for MoHUA.

s: In Swachh Survekshan 2024-25, Indore led the Super Swachh League for the:
x: Indore has been the cleanest city eight times.

s: Which city topped the new Swachh Shahar category (10 lakh+) in Swachh Survekshan 2024-25?
x: Ahmedabad topped the new Swachh Shahar 10 lakh+ category, ahead of Bhopal and Lucknow.

s: How many cities were covered by Swachh Survekshan 2024-25?
x: Swachh Survekshan began in 2016 with 73 cities and covered 4,589 in 2024-25.

s: Which city topped the Super Swachh League for cities of 3-10 lakh population in Swachh Survekshan 2024-25?
x: Noida led the 3-10 lakh Super Swachh League, followed by Chandigarh and Mysuru; Indore led the 10 lakh+ league.

s: In the Human Development Report 2025, India's HDI value of 0.685 places it in which category?
x: 0.685 lies in the Medium band (0.550-0.699), just below the 0.700 threshold for High. Low is below 0.550, and Very high is 0.800 and above, so neither applies.

s: Which two persistent weaknesses of India were flagged in the HDR 2025?
o: Low life expectancy and low school enrolment
x: The report identified gender inequality and income inequality as India's two persistent weaknesses.

s: The Human Development Report 2025 placed India at which position among countries and territories?
x: India was ranked 130th among 193 countries and territories in the Human Development Report 2025.

s: Which of the following groups consists only of countries ranked above India in the HDR 2025?
x: China, Sri Lanka and Bhutan were listed above India, with ranks 78, 89 and 125 respectively. Bangladesh had the same rank of 130 in the cited comparison.

s: Which pair of Human Development Report edition and India's rank is correctly matched?
x: India was 132nd in HDR 2021-22; it was 119th in HDR 2010, 129th in HDR 2019 and 134th in HDR 2023-24.

s: Which neighbouring country shared India's rank of 130 in the HDR 2025?
x: Bangladesh shares rank 130 with India; Sri Lanka (89) and Bhutan (125) are ahead and Nepal (145) is below.

s: What was Sri Lanka's HDI rank in the HDR 2025?
x: Sri Lanka ranked 89, ahead of India (130); China was 78 and Nepal 145.

s: Which country ranked first in the Human Development Report 2025?
x: Iceland topped the HDR 2025 with an HDI of 0.972; South Sudan was last (193rd).

s: Which country has the highest life expectancy as per the HDR 2025?
x: Japan has the highest life expectancy, while Iceland ranked first overall.

s: Which country was ranked last (193rd) in the HDR 2025?
x: South Sudan was ranked last, 193rd, in the HDR 2025.

s: What was India's HDI value in the Human Development Report 2021-22?
x: In HDR 2021-22 India had an HDI of 0.633 and was ranked 132 of 191.

s: What was India's life expectancy at birth as per the Human Development Report 2025?
x: HDR 2025 gives India a life expectancy of 72 years and expected years of schooling of 13 years.

s: What was India's rank in the Human Development Report 2023-24?
x: India was ranked 134 of 193 in HDR 2023-24; it was 132 in 2021-22 and 130 in 2025.

s: Which of India's neighbours had the highest HDI rank in the Human Development Report 2025?
x: China was ranked 78, ahead of Sri Lanka (89) and Bhutan (125).

s: What was India's rank in the Gender Inequality Index of the Human Development Report 2025?
x: HDR 2025 ranked India 102nd of 193 in the GII, up from 108th; its GDI value is 0.874.

s: How many countries were ranked in the Human Development Report 2018?
x: The HDR 2018 ranked 189 countries; later reports ranked 191 and then 193.

s: Since 2010, which method is used to combine the three dimension indices of the HDI?
x: The HDI is the geometric mean of the three indices, which replaced the arithmetic mean in 2010.

s: Which indicator measures the income dimension of the HDI?
x: HDI uses GNI per capita; education uses mean years of schooling (25+) and expected years of schooling.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a component of the Human Development Index?
x: The HDI combines life expectancy at birth (health), mean and expected years of schooling (knowledge) and GNI per capita (income). Military expenditure, like inequality, poverty and gender gaps, is not part of the HDI; inequality is captured separately by the IHDI.

s: What are the goalposts used for life expectancy at birth in the HDI?
x: The health dimension uses life expectancy at birth with goalposts of 20 and 85 years.

s:
Consider the following statements about the HDI knowledge dimension:
1. Mean years of schooling is measured for adults aged 25 and above.
2. Expected years of schooling has a goalpost of 0–18 years.
3. Adult literacy rate is still one of its indicators.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: MYS (adults 25+, goalpost 0–15) and EYS (0–18) measure knowledge; literacy was replaced by them in 2010.

s: From which HDI value does a country enter the 'High human development' category?
x: High human development is 0.700–0.799; 0.800 and above is Very High.

s: What is the maximum goalpost (cap) for GNI per capita (PPP) in the HDI?
x: GNI per capita (PPP, log) is capped at $75,000 in the HDI.

s: Below which HDI value is a country placed in the 'Low human development' category?
x: Countries with an HDI below 0.550 are in the Low category; 0.550-0.699 is Medium.

s: In which year did Amartya Sen receive the Nobel Prize in Economics?
x: Sen received the Nobel in 1998; the human development approach views development as the enlargement of human choices.

s: How are capabilities described in Amartya Sen's capability approach?
o: Substantive freedoms to lead lives people value
Rise in per capita national income
Fixed universal list of basic needs
x: Sen defined capabilities as substantive freedoms to lead the lives people value and avoided a fixed universal list.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Human Development Reports:
1. They are published by the World Bank.
2. The first Human Development Report was published in 1990.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is wrong: the HDRs are published by the UNDP, not the World Bank. Statement 2 is correct: the first HDR came out in 1990. So '2 only'; '1 only' and 'Both' wrongly accept statement 1, and 'Neither' rejects the correct statement 2.

s: In which year was Amartya Sen's book 'Development as Freedom' published?
x: 'Development as Freedom' came out in 1999; 1990 is the year of the first HDR, conceived by Mahbub ul Haq with Sen.

s: What is the title of the Human Development Report 2025?
o: Beyond Income: Human Development in a Changing World
People, Prosperity and Planet in the Digital Age
A Matter of Choice: People and Possibilities in the Age of AI
Human Development and the Future of Work
x: The HDR 2025 is titled “A Matter of Choice: People and Possibilities in the Age of AI”.

s: Who is the Pakistani economist who conceived the Human Development Report?
x: Mahbub ul Haq, a Pakistani economist, conceived the HDR, which he co-conceived with Amartya Sen.

s: The Global Multidimensional Poverty Index is prepared by UNDP together with which institution?
o: Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)
x: The MPI measures deprivations in health, education and living standards and is prepared by UNDP and OPHI.

s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh had the lowest multidimensional poverty headcount ratio (2.42 per cent)?
x: West Godavari had the lowest ratio at 2.42 per cent; AP's MPI halved from 0.053 to 0.025.

s: Which sequence correctly identifies the first Human Development Report and the first National Human Development Report of India?
x: The first Human Development Report was published in 1990, while India’s first National Human Development Report was published in 2001.

s: According to NITI Aayog (January 2024), multidimensional poverty in India fell from 29.17% in 2013-14 to what level?
x: NITI Aayog reported a fall from 29.17% to 11.28%, with 24.82 crore people moving out of poverty.

s: Which State recorded the biggest fall in the number of multidimensionally poor (2013-14 to 2022-23)?
x: Uttar Pradesh saw the biggest fall (5.94 crore), followed by Bihar and Madhya Pradesh.

s: Which body prepared the first National Human Development Report of India (2001)?
x: The first NHDR (2001) was brought out by the Planning Commission and released on 23 April 2002; Kerala was top.

s: Which State topped the first National Human Development Report of India?
x: Kerala was ranked top in the first NHDR (2001).

s: Which two States have a state HDI above 0.86 in the sub-national series?
x: Kerala and Goa are above 0.86, while Bihar is lowest at 0.650.

s: What was the national multidimensional poverty headcount ratio, against Andhra Pradesh's 6.06%?
x: AP's headcount of 6.06% is well below the national 14.96%; AP's MPI halved from 0.053 to 0.025.

s: In the sub-national HDI series, which State has the lowest HDI (0.650)?
x: Bihar is lowest at 0.650 in the sub-national series (India 0.732; not comparable with UNDP's 0.685); Kerala and Goa are above 0.86.

s: As per the National Human Development Report 2001, which State had the lowest HDI?
x: Bihar was at the bottom of the first NHDR (2001), while Kerala was at the top.

s:
Consider the following statements about the first National Human Development Report of India:
1. It was prepared by the Planning Commission and released in April 2002.
2. Andhra Pradesh was at the top of it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The first NHDR (2001) was prepared by the Planning Commission and released on 23 April 2002; Kerala, not Andhra Pradesh, was at the top.

s: According to NITI Aayog (January 2024), how many people in India moved out of multidimensional poverty between 2013-14 and 2022-23?
x: NITI Aayog said 24.82 crore people moved out of multidimensional poverty; 5.94 crore of them were in UP.

s: Which method does NITI Aayog use to compute India's national Multidimensional Poverty Index?
x: The national MPI uses 12 indicators and the Alkire-Foster method.

s: Andhra Pradesh's MPI value halved from 0.053 in 2015-16 to what level in 2019-21?
x: AP's MPI value fell from 0.053 to 0.025, roughly half.

s: How many indicators are used in India's national Multidimensional Poverty Index of NITI Aayog?
x: NITI Aayog's national MPI uses 12 indicators and the Alkire-Foster method.

s: Which State has the lowest Multidimensional Poverty Index value (0.002)?
x: Kerala has the lowest MPI (0.002) and Bihar the highest (0.16).

s: As per the National Human Development Report 2001, what was India's HDI value?
x: The NHDR 2001 put India's HDI at 0.472, up from 0.381 in 1991.

s: What was the rank of Andhra Pradesh among the States in the HDI of the National Human Development Report 2001?
x: The NHDR 2001 placed Andhra Pradesh 10th among the States, below the national average.

s: Which institution prepared the India Human Development Report 2011?
o: National Council of Applied Economic Research
Centre for Economic and Social Studies
x: The India Human Development Report 2011 was prepared by the Institute of Applied Manpower Research of the Planning Commission; Kerala topped it.

s: Unlike human development, which has both quantitative and qualitative dimensions, what is economic growth primarily?
x: Economic growth is primarily quantitative and associated with income.

s: Where inequality exists in a country, how does its Inequality-adjusted HDI (IHDI) compare with its HDI?
x: The IHDI discounts the HDI for inequality in each dimension, so it is lower when inequality exists and equals the HDI only when there is none.

s: The Human Poverty Index was the forerunner of which index?
x: The Human Poverty Index preceded and served as the forerunner of the Multidimensional Poverty Index.

s: Which of the following pairs about the Human Development Index is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Health – Included as an HDI dimension
Education – Included as an HDI dimension
Inequality – A criticism: not reflected in the HDI
Sustainability – Included as an HDI dimension
x: The HDI includes health and education; one of its criticisms is that it ignores sustainability, along with inequality, gender and political freedom.

s: Which index is the ratio of female to male HDI?
x: GDI is the female-to-male HDI ratio; GII covers reproductive health, empowerment and labour market; PQLI uses literacy, infant mortality and life expectancy.

s: In the Gender Inequality Index (GII), what does a value of 0 denote?
o: maximum inequality between women and men
female HDI higher than male HDI
male HDI higher than female HDI
x: On the GII scale, 0 = equality and 1 = worst outcome; the GDI (female-to-male HDI ratio) near 1 means parity.

s: Which index is described as HDI discounted for inequality?
x: The IHDI discounts the HDI for inequality; the gap between HDI and IHDI is the loss due to inequality.

s: Which indicators were used in the Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI), a pre-HDI measure?
x: The PQLI combined literacy, infant mortality and life expectancy before the HDI was introduced.
